name: Espressif
description: Xtensa architectures for the ESP8266, ESP32, ESP32-S2 and ESP32-S3, and firmware, ELF, ROM symbol and SVD loading for those and the RISC-V ESP32-C2, C3, C6, H2 and C5
longdescription:
A Binary Ninja plugin for Espressif chips: Xtensa architectures for the ESP8266, ESP32, ESP32-S2 and ESP32-S3 (disassembly in GNU objdump syntax and lifting of the whole ISA), and loading of Espressif firmware images, flash dumps, ELF files, ROM symbols and SVD files for those chips and the RISC-V ESP32-C2, C3, C6, H2 and C5.

The plugin is a native (Rust) library. The extension manager installs a small Python loader that installs the prebuilt native library matching your Binary Ninja (Linux x86_64, Windows x86_64 or macOS). Releases are currently built for the core ABI of the Binary Ninja dev channel at release time; stable support will come later. If your Binary Ninja's core ABI doesn't match, the loader says so and installs nothing.

The loader:

- In the UI, it asks before downloading the library from this plugin's GitHub release, and asks again only for a new version. Plugins > Espressif also has commands to install, update or remove it.
- Headless, it downloads only if the `espressif.loader.autoDownload` setting is enabled.
- The download is accepted only if its SHA-256 matches the hash committed in the plugin's source. It is copied into the user plugin folder as `binja_espressif-native.so` / `.dll` / `.dylib`; restart Binary Ninja to load it.
- If the plugin folder already has a library you built yourself, the loader leaves it alone.

This plugin was called binja-xtensa ("Espressif Xtensa") up to 0.1.0-rc.3; the extension manager lists it as a separate plugin. Install this one, uninstall Espressif Xtensa and restart: the loader installs nothing while Espressif Xtensa is installed, and then replaces its native library (`binja_xtensa-native`), so only one copy loads.

Uninstalling the plugin in the extension manager does not remove the native library: run Plugins > Espressif > Remove Native Library first, or delete the file from the user plugin folder.

See https://github.com/jrozner/binja-espressif for details and for building from source.

installinstructions.Darwin: Requires a dev build of Binary Ninja (stable is not supported yet). Install with the extension manager, then accept the prompt to download the native library (or use Plugins > Espressif > Install or Update Native Library; headless, enable espressif.loader.autoDownload) and restart Binary Ninja. To uninstall, run Plugins > Espressif > Remove Native Library before removing the plugin.
